headline: Approved Hanover Street sidewalk/parking redesign 8-6 despite objections; rejected 79-E tax relief for 959 Elm Street
summary: The board heard extensive public comment on the Hanover Street pedestrian improvement project, school district budget concerns, and a proposed RAISE TIF district for the southern millyard bridge project. After debate, the board approved the Hanover Street parking regulation changes by roll call vote, denied a Community Revitalization Tax Relief (79-E) application for 959 Elm Street, and approved numerous budget resolutions and committee reports including CIP fund transfers, personnel changes, and traffic regulations.
decisions: Voted to take all public comments under advisement and receive and file written documentation presented.
Voted to waive the reading of the Hanover Street committee report.
Approved the Hanover Street parking regulation changes with the stipulation that regulations not take effect until construction is about to commence, roll call 8-6.
Voted to confirm nominations to the Board of Adjustment, Planning Board, and Retirement Board as presented.
Voted to confirm Aldermanic nominations to the Manchester Public Television Service as presented.
Voted to accept with regret the retirement communication from Central Fleet Services Director Richard Bilodeau.
Denied the application for a Community Revitalization Tax Relief Incentive (RSA 79-E) for 959 Elm Street, roll call vote with Mayor voting nay, motion failed.
Voted to receive and file the Livingston Basketball Court Project item rather than refer it to Committee on Lands and Buildings, with Alderman O'Neil opposed.
Voted to recess the meeting to allow the Committee on Finance to meet.
Accepted the Committee on Finance report and adopted its recommendations (multiple CIP fund resolutions) ought to pass and be Enrolled.
Accepted the Committee on Public Safety, Health & Traffic report approving re-delegation of authority to Planning and Community Development to issue certain building attachment permits, unanimous.

Passed and enrolled a series of Resolutions amending FY2022-2026 Community Improvement Programs for various projects including Healthy Food Access, MHRA Landlord Incentive, Odd Fellows Hall, ARPA Coordinator, Part Time Planner, Independent City Auditor, CDBG-CV shelter support, Opioid Abatement, Safe Haven Baby Box, Women's Locker Room Expansion, MPD Mobile Surveillance Platform, and Homeless Healthcare.
Passed and ordained an Ordinance amending Section 33.026 (Equipment Operator III, IV, and V) of the Code of Ordinances.
A motion to amend the December 5, 2023 school facility bond resolution failed for lack of a second.
Voted to refer the snow removal ordinance/sidewalk responsibility conflict item to the Committee on Public Safety, Health & Traffic.
